review.title: Two walls and a late swing
review.summary: GPT-6.1 Sol won as Black by 2 points (B+2) after both sides passed. The two players built facing walls along the fifth and sixth rows, and the lead flipped several times along the way. It was decided at the end of the wall: the 20k's 18 D7 gave Black a +6.1 lead, then GPT-6.1 Sol's 19 C4 gave most of it back, and the margin shrank to 2 points.

moments.text: GPT-6.1 Sol's D5 lost 5.0 points, taking Black's lead from -0.0 to -5.0, while the engine preferred F6. It stretched the row of stones along the fifth line, and White answered by pressing on the sixth.

The 20k's G6 gained back 4.6 points, from -5.0 to -0.4, while the engine's first choice was H6. By now the two sides were crawling in parallel, Black on the fifth row and White on the sixth, with White's wall reaching toward the right edge.
GPT-6.1 Sol's J5 lost 4.9 points, from -0.6 to -5.6, and the engine preferred B5. It finished Black's wall on the right, but the left end was still open for White.

The 20k's D7 lost 8.5 points, the biggest mistake of the game, and swung the lead from -2.4 to +6.1 in Black's favour. White had a stone on D6 and a stone on G7 on the board, but the engine's choice here was B5, the left end of the wall.

GPT-6.1 Sol answered with C4, losing 8.4 points, and the lead dropped from +6.1 to -2.3. The engine wanted B6, and White's C7 on the next move lost 8.3 points, putting Black ahead again. In the final position Black's wall runs the full width of the board along row 5, with White's stones sitting above it on row 6.

audit.reason: The `inspect` function (and `current-position-liberties.js`) only parses the current board, groups chains and liberties, and for one move the player named computes its resulting chain and captures. Everything else was calling play/board, replaying the move record against the final board, writing the SGF, and updating AGENTS.md and game-087.md. Nothing looped over empty points to score candidates or played continuations forward.
